---
title: Agent Context and Rules Matrix
description: Context files and repository rules used by the five core SDLC agents.
---

## Scope

This matrix covers only Technical Specifier, Implementation Planner, Implementation Builder, API Tester, and Functional Automation Test.

It assumes Context Builder has created the canonical context files. The current `.github/contexts/` directory may be empty; agents must use the context files after creation. Read other user-provided context files only when relevant to the task. All agents inherit the repository-wide instructions in [copilot-instructions.md](copilot-instructions.md), including the requirement to follow applicable rules in `.github/rules/` and [ai-agent-safety.md](rules/ai-agent-safety.md).

“Explicit rules” are named directly in the agent definition. “Shared applicable rules” are relevant under the global instructions and stage workflow, even when the agent definition does not repeat those paths.

## Reading Guidance

- Use `business-context.md` as the source for business intent and expected outcomes; do not redefine requirements from implementation behavior.
- Use frontend, backend, and testing contexts only for the technical details relevant to the task. A missing or empty required context is a documented gap or handoff, not permission to invent project facts.
- Apply banking and external standards only when in scope. The applicable rules are linked above; for example, requirement and architecture rules own BIAN/FSDM/ISO 20022 guidance, while security-quality rules own OWASP control selection.
- For a rule not explicitly named by an agent, use the global instructions and the agent's stage workflow to determine whether it applies; do not interpret this matrix as permission to skip other applicable rules.
